https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.question: How should a person act responsibly when certainty is unavailable?
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.thesis: Academic skepticism treats persuasive, revisable judgments as adequate grounds for action without elevating them to unquestionable truth.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.argument: Human senses and reasoning are fallible. If certainty is required before action, practical life stalls; if conviction is equated with truth, correction becomes impossible. The plausible supplies a graded middle position.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.intellectual_background: Arcesilaus and Carneades developed the skeptical New Academy; Cicero carried its ideas into Roman practical philosophy.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.example: A public-health official may act on the best available evidence while publicly specifying what would reverse the recommendation.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.strongest_objection: Plausibility can become a cover for prejudice or arbitrary judgment when standards are weak.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.possible_response: The approach demands comparison of rival arguments and an explicit willingness to revise, rather than treating intuition alone as sufficient.
https://aeon.co/essays/a-good-sceptic-ha.implications: Better decisions should specify confidence, alternatives and reversal conditions.
